title: Speculative decode scaffolding: kernel-aware routing, early-output validators, and rollback choreography
creator: Aisha Menon
description:
Objective: Implement a lightweight speculative decode scaffolding in the serving runtime that supports kernel-aware model routing for tentative outputs, an early-output validator that estimates acceptance confidence, and a rollback choreography to safely retract tentative outputs when validation fails. This ticket covers design and an MVP implementation (canary) for host and dedicated modes.

Motivation: Many workloads benefit from speculative execution that returns lower-latency candidate tokens from smaller/faster kernels or quantized model variants while the full decode completes. We need a predictable, observable mechanism to route requests to tentative paths, estimate whether tentative outputs are acceptable, and retract them deterministically when they are not. Current codebase has probe-prefill and acceptance playbooks spread across multiple modules; this work consolidates a minimal runtime shim and operational contract to reduce complexity and improve telemetry coverage.
background_notes: Existing patterns in runtime: prefills, prober, handoff. These are scattered in decode orchestration and kernel scheduler modules.
Constraints: must not change public API, must preserve per-request determinism for auditing, and cannot increase P50 latency for steady-state full-decode requests.
Assumption: small/fast model variants or lower-precision kernels provide early tokens that are often but not always acceptable; we will treat them as tentative until validator confirms.
Non-goal: full bandit-style model selection, multi-armed bandit tuning, or offline continuous learning. MVP is rule-driven and telemetry-first.
design_summary: Introduce a SpeculateShim layer between router and decode conductor that: (1) consults a KernelAffinity table to choose candidate fast kernels/variants, (2) dispatches a tentative decode path with reduced compute budget to produce an early token sequence, (3) runs an EarlyOutputValidator micro-policy that scores textual outputs against request-level heuristics (prompt coherence, safety heuristics, log-prob delta, special token signals), and (4) on validator failure triggers a deterministic rollback event which replaces the tentative output with the canonical decode result. The shim will expose metrics and events used by Console rollouts and Optimize suggestions.
acceptance_criteria: SpeculateShim integrated into runtime with feature flag runtime.speculative_mvp = true
KernelAffinity config supports per-model candidate lists and score weights (mutable via config service)
EarlyOutputValidator emits a numeric confidence [0.0-1.0] and a discrete decision: accept | reject | defer

Rollback choreography ensures client-visible output is deterministic: if tentative is rejected, final output replaces tentative and clients observe a consistent token stream via existing streaming semantics (no duplicated tokens or broken ordering)

Telemetry: counters for candidate_used, validator_confidence_histogram, rollback_count, rollback_reasons, end_to_end_latency_delta; these are exported to Console with per-route and per-model breakdown

Unit + integration tests cover: validator heuristics, kernel affinity selection, rollback mechanism under simulated race conditions, and load tests to show no regression in P50 for standard decode flows by more than 3%
Canary rollout plan documented and validated with synthetic and real traffic in dedicated region before full rollout
detailed_plan: Phase 1 (Design + config): finalize KernelAffinity schema, validator heuristics, and rollback contract. Deliver config proto and feature flag gating.
Phase 2 (Runtime shim): implement SpeculateShim that can dispatch parallel tentative decode on an affinity kernel and attach an outcome token envelope to the request context.

Phase 3 (Validator + rollback): implement EarlyOutputValidator module and rollback choreography that can atomically retract tentative tokens and replace with canonical stream while preserving token indices.
Phase 4 (Observability): add metrics, traces, and event logs for every speculative decision and expose a Console dashboard query template for early monitoring.

Phase 5 (Canary): enable in a single low-traffic region for 48 hours, compare quality/regression metrics and operational signals, iterate heuristics, then expand to Dedicated customers behind an opt-in flag.
Phase 6 (Docs + SDKs): document behavior for SDKs about potential tentative tokens and provide client-side hints to handle retractions gracefully (idempotent token stream markers).
tradeoffs: Validator heuristics vs. model-based acceptance: heuristics are faster and simpler for MVP but will have false positives/negatives; future work could replace with learned acceptors.
Parallel tentative decode increases peak GPU usage; mitigated by limiting candidate list to 1 fast variant and using low compute budgets for tentative path.
Rollback introduces complexity for streaming semantics; chosen approach is atomic replacement to avoid partial client-visible reorders but requires careful client compatibility testing.
KernelAffinity config is flexible but could be misconfigured by operators; add conservative defaults and safe-fail behavior (disable speculative path if misconfigured).
telemetry_and_sla: Emit per-request event 'speculative.decision' with fields: model, kernel_variant, validator_confidence, decision, rollback_reason (if any)
Alerts: rollback_rate > 3% for a route or model triggers SEV-2 investigation; end_to_end_quality_regression > 1% triggers rollback of feature flag
SLO impact: ensure 99th percentile latency for full-decode unchanged; track speculative path tail separately and cap resource usage so as not to violate Dedicated capacity guarantees
testing_plan: Unit tests for KernelAffinity selection logic and validator heuristics boundary cases
Integration tests that spin up in-memory runtime and simulate concurrent tentative and canonical decodes validating rollback correctness
Chaos tests: inject delays and GPU throttling to ensure rollback still preserves deterministic output ordering
A/B evaluation with synthetic prompts and human-labeled quality checks comparing tentative acceptance vs final output
Load test on staging to measure peak GPU memory and latency impact with speculative enabled at 10% of traffic
operational_runbook: Feature flag runtime.speculative_mvp default off. Enable per-namespace via Console for canary.
If rollback_rate exceeds threshold: disable feature flag, gather last 5k speculative.decision events for failing route, engage runtime and model teams
If streaming clients observe duplicated tokens: cut flag and run trace on affected request IDs to debug ordering bug
Escalation path: on large customer impact (>= 10% of requests affected), contact on-call infra and customer success immediately
